newsitem.title: MEXICO: British agriculture minister visits Mexico.
newsitem.headline: British agriculture minister visits Mexico.

text.p: Britain's junior agriculture minister Tony Baldry began a five-day visit to Mexico Monday, saying he expected to see greater British investment in Mexican agriculture in the future.

Baldry, who is on a Latin American tour which will take him to Brazil, Argentina and Peru, also reiterated Britain's support for improved terms for Mexico regarding access to the European Union's single market under a free-trade pact now under discussion.

"We see enormous potential for investment and partnership in whole areas of agriculture, horticulture and fisheries," Baldry told a news conference. "Britain is the second-biggest overseas investor in Mexico, a position we intend to maintain."
"I think Mexico will find the United Kingdom a firm advocate" for greater access to the European Union than some other EU nations currently propose, he added.

He estimated British investment in the last few years in the Mexican agriculture sector at about $500,000, mostly from big firms, but added he expected medium- and small-sized firms with specialized technology to invest more in the coming years.

Baldry, who will meet Mexican Agriculture Minister Francisco Labastida, will also travel to the states of Baja California, Colima, Jalisco, Sinaloa and Chihuahua with a delegation of British businessmen.
